close_reason:
Closing as opinion / no engineering basis to change.

The current form `let _ = (inner, type_name, account_id);` in the realistic-demo-ids cfg branch is a documented Rust idiom for explicit discard, scoped tightly to the branch where the params are unused.

The bead's two proposed alternatives both have downsides:
(a) Underscore-prefix the params and split into two cfg-branched function definitions — doubles the function signature for marginal clarity gain.
(b) `#[cfg_attr(feature = "realistic-demo-ids", allow(unused_variables))]` on the function — applies the lint allowance to the whole function including the (not(realistic-demo-ids)) branch where the params ARE used; less precise than the in-branch discard.

The bead author labeled this opinion + clippy + idiomatic-rust acknowledging it as cosmetic. Stopping here per the workspace bikeshedding-signal rule: "Only flag things that have an engineering basis that would survive a code review comment thread." The current form is acceptable Rust and clippy does not complain (verified by the recent `cargo clippy -p jmap-calendars-server -- -D warnings` clean exit during JMAP-ic0j.48 work).
title: demo_next_id 'realistic' branch uses 'let _ = (a, b, c)' triple-binding discard
